scorecards.inningsCommentary: Australia commenced their first innings at Perth Stadium, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 70 from MS Harris, complemented by a commanding 112-run stand between MS Harris and AJ Finch that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.99 RPO. India's bowling response was spearheaded by Ishant Sharma (4/40), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 326/10 (108.3 ov), Australia posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: India embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 287 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. Ajinkya Rahane anchored the innings with a resolute 30, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. Australia's bowling response was spearheaded by Nathan Lyon (3/39), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Dismissed for 140/10 (55.7 ov), India succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as Australia's bowlers closed out the victory.

summaryTab.matchStory: Australia posted 326 in the opening innings with MS Harris (70) providing key resistance. India replied strongly with 283, powered by Virat Kohli's commanding century (123) to swing the contest. Australia posted 243 in their second innings, shifting match momentum decisively through crucial partnerships. Australia's bowling attack dismantled India for 140 in the fourth innings to complete the win.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Perth Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Australia posted 326/10 (108.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, India countered with 283/10 (105.5 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Mohammed Shami (6/54), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Nathan Lyon delivered a masterclass for Australia (14 Runs & 8 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Australia 47%) and allowing Australia to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, India faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Australia's bowling unit, bolstered by Virat Kohli (140 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Australia won by 146 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Australia's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While India produced fighting phases, Australia won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
